items.title: Armature.tech analyzes 17,000 coding agent runs to compare tool choices by Claude, Codex, and Cursor across 75 simulated repositories [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Which tools do Claude, Codex and Cursor choose? We measured 17k runs to find out
items.summary:
Armature.tech conducted an extensive study of 16,893 coding agent runs, focusing on 5,292 valid sessions across 75 simulated repositories in 10 programming languages to understand how AI agents Claude, Codex, and Cursor select tools for real-world coding tasks. The experiments involved diverse developer personas and realistic prompts, with a simulated human in the loop to guide tool selection and implementation decisions.

The study found that different coding agents rely on distinct information sources: Cursor uses web data in two-thirds of sessions, Codex almost always performs focused web searches, and Claude primarily depends on its internal knowledge but browses more pages when it searches. The results reveal varying preferences and strategies among agents, with detailed traces made publicly available for further analysis.

items.title: Developer ports 1993 Amiga game Babylonian Twins to Godot using an LLM to interpret original 68000 assembly code [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Porting my 1993 Amiga game to Godot, with an LLM reading the 68000 assembly
items.summary:
A developer has ported the 1993 Amiga game Babylonian Twins to the Godot engine by leveraging a large language model (LLM) to read and interpret the original 68000 assembly code. The game, originally built under challenging conditions in Baghdad with direct hardware programming and limited resources, was reconstructed with AI assistance to translate decades-old binary level maps and assembly into modern code.

The process involved running the LLM in an environment with access to the original toolchain and filesystem, enabling it to assemble, build, and test the game automatically. This approach allowed the AI to handle complex tasks such as reading binary formats and rebuilding the game logic at the Amiga's original 50 Hz frame rate, significantly speeding up the porting compared to previous manual efforts. The project demonstrates the potential of AI to assist in preserving and modernizing legacy software.

Each company reported elevated error rates or user-facing issues, with some resolving the problems within a few hours while others continued to work on restoring service.

Anthropic reported partial outages on multiple Claude versions starting at 9:23 a.m. Eastern, resolving by early afternoon. OpenAI noted degraded performance on ChatGPT and Codex beginning at 10:43 a.m., with mitigation completed by 12:55 p.m. xAI's Grok showed significant user error reports starting before 9:45 a.m., and Google’s Gemini experienced a likely API outage between 10:45 and 11:15 a.m. Despite these AI model issues, major cloud providers like AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Cloudflare did not report major disruptions during this period.

Such overlapping downtime across leading AI models is highly unusual given their typical high uptime rates, with Claude and ChatGPT both reporting over 99% uptime in recent months. This incident highlights the challenges of maintaining continuous availability in complex AI services even among top providers.

items.summary:
We’re getting ready for Anthropic to make its initial public offering prospectus public sometime after Labor Day. Though the company’s private investors have had a window into its torrid growth and projections, this will be the first time public investors are getting a full financial picture of the Claude maker. 

Just how complete a picture remains a big question, though. We’re hearing that investors want a lot more from Anthropic than the financial statements that securities regulators generally require companies to report.

These include AI tokenomics, including what it makes off every AI token it processes, how much revenue it’s generating per gigawatt of compute, and net revenue retention, a measure of a tech vendor’s ability to keep customers and increase their spending. There’s no guarantee Anthropic will provide any of these.
